identity.name: Sodium carbonates (sodium carbonate, sodium hydrogen carbonate, sodium sesquicarbonate)

function.mechanism: Carbonate/bicarbonate buffering neutralizes acids and controls pH; bicarbonate-containing forms can release CO2 in acid/heat conditions, supporting leavening.

adi.basis: No numeric EFSA ADI published in current ongoing E500(i)-E500(iii) re-evaluation records (EFSA-Q-2011-00648/00649/00650).

efsa.key_finding: Open EFSA records show E500(i), E500(ii), and E500(iii) in ongoing risk assessment (last updated 2026-01-19); comments state these additives are already authorised in the EU and re-evaluation is delayed, with a new data call expected in 2026/2027.

adi.basis: JECFA descriptor ADIs: NOT LIMITED (sodium carbonate; sodium bicarbonate) and NOT SPECIFIED (sodium sesquicarbonate).

concerns.summary: Some clinical meta-analytic data in CKD populations report increased diastolic pressure and higher risk of worsening hypertension/edema with oral sodium bicarbonate supplementation.
High supplemental doses can cause gastrointestinal intolerance (e.g., in sports dosing studies).
Excessive non-food-pattern ingestion can cause severe metabolic alkalosis and hypernatremia; review identified multiple toxicity cases tied to misuse.

no_concern_confirmed: FDA CFR sections affirm sodium carbonate, sodium bicarbonate, and sodium sesquicarbonate as GRAS for direct food use under current good manufacturing practice.
JECFA evaluations report low-concern descriptor ADIs (NOT LIMITED / NOT SPECIFIED) rather than a restrictive numeric ADI.
IARC monograph search did not identify a classification entry for sodium carbonate, sodium bicarbonate, or sodium sesquicarbonate.

adi_exceedance.notes: No numeric EFSA or JECFA mg/kg bw/day ADI was identified for E500 components in current records; exceedance cannot be calculated in the usual numeric way. Risk signals are dose-pattern dependent and mainly associated with high supplemental/misuse exposure.

risk_assessment.rationale: Regulatory evidence supports low concern under normal food-use conditions (FDA GRAS; JECFA not limited/not specified descriptors), while adverse findings are mainly linked to high supplemental or misuse exposure patterns. EFSA re-evaluation remains ongoing, which adds uncertainty but does not currently indicate withdrawal.
key_factors: FDA GRAS status with GMP-based use conditions in 21 CFR 184.1736, 184.1742, and 184.1792
JECFA descriptor ADIs (NOT LIMITED / NOT SPECIFIED) for E500 components
No IARC monograph classification entry found for these compounds
Adverse effects observed primarily in high-dose supplementation or misuse contexts
